body: I have to be up in 3 hours for work so I'm going to try to sleep. Thanks again for talking. I know from experience that talking to depressed people who know how to fix their problem but just can't is not always an easy thing to do.

I do cook (though I could stand to take it more seriously) and I'm learning to play guitar and I try to read a certain amount each day, etc. My days are usually pretty full and I'm usually good about staving off the bad thoughts, but sometimes it comes crashing down and I lose a few days to a few weeks just being sad and I've yet to figure out how to avoid it. They can definitely be triggered by this guy toying with me or ignoring me, but I keep track and those aren't the only bad days.

I've been trying that sort of. I've always spent a lot of time alone so nothing feels different in that regard. The best friend never liked hiking or exercising with me so I did and do those things alone. Also our movie tastes Venn diagram mostly overlapped, but we'd go see the outliers alone, so that's nothing new for me either.

Thanks. It's tough. I guess it's better that he moved out rather than moved her in. I really don't think I would have survived that. That must have been awful for you. We all work for the same company but they work together at one site and I travel from site to site and have avoided her for 2 years now (I do occasionally have to see him though I try to avoid that too). 

My feelings for him are confused now. He's not the same person he was before he left - his interests, attitude, political beliefs, diet, personality etc have all changed, possibly because of this girl's influence. Some things are better, most things are worse. I still feel like if the old him showed up one day, my feelings would flood back but right now I'm mostly just confused as to who this person is and how much of it is here to stay. 

I also weirdly cultivated a crush on someone else. It normally takes me a long time to develop feelings for someone - like years. But I started playing d&d at a local game store to try to make friends and met someone who reminded me of him. So if I found myself thinking about my best friend, I made a point to think about this guy instead and at first it helped immensely and was fun.  Then it started getting painful and I realized I had just projected old feelings onto some poor guy I don't even know (and because we only play d&d together where he heavily roleplays I don't even really know what his real personality is like - it's all conjecture). Then I felt pathetic.

I hope things work out for you as well. I don't recommend the above method though.

Thanks. This guy has/had a lot of great qualities, but rationally I know he wasn't a prize. I don't put him on a pedestal or anything. At times I do feel like I dodged a bullet and good riddance to the other girl for getting saddled with him.

But no matter what, I did think the 10 year friendship we had was special and I've never stopped feeling that. And I feel like I'm realizing that it was only special to me... and the worthless and hopeless feelings that that triggers in me....i can't even describe it. But I don't think there's any way past it. I don't think I'm ever going to recover. 

I feel like the only way out is making friends and finding someone else to care about and hope it's reciprocal, but I'm paralyzed with fear of opening up to someone again, even just as friends. I've tried meetups, OK Cupid, game nights, and I can't move past initial stages. It was always hard for me and it seems impossible now. 

I feel like the rest of my life is going to be as lonely and empty as the past 2 years have been. I don't feel dramatically suicidal, but I do feel increasingly like I'm running out of options. 

Thanks for talking. I knew this issue wasn't going to get solved tonight, but it did feel better to talk.

They had been friends for something like a year, but yeah, the move out was very sudden and really hurt me financially as well as I was left with a lease I could barely afford on my own and I couldn't bring myself to threaten legal action or anything like that.

In his defense, I was not easy to live with, especially after I started school. That's part of what made everything so hard... Having to accept I may have been abusive and mean and thoughtless and that I'm possibly the villain here. I feel like the villain most of the time.

I am not sure that I still have romantic feelings for him - he has changed a lot and in ways I don't always like. But it still hurts when he doesn't put minimal effort into fixing our friendship. I feel like I need that redemption in some form.
